title: HTTP caching: Cache-Control, ETag and 304
summary: With Cache-Control the server states whether a response can be stored, who can store it and for how long.

sections.definition: With Cache-Control the server states whether a response can be stored, who can store it and for how long. When it expires, the client revalidates with If-None-Match, sending the ETag; if it did not change, the server responds 304 Not Modified with no body.
sections.analogy: The menu of the day written on a board. If it says "valid until 3 p.m." (max-age), you do not ask again. After 3 you ask: "Is it still menu version 7?" (If-None-Match). If they tell you "yes, the same one" (304), they do not read you the whole menu again.
sections.problem: It avoids work and traffic: without caching, every user downloads the same catalog over and over. Misused it is dangerous: marking a response with user data as public can make a CDN serve Pedro the orders of Ana. For private data you use private or no-store.
sections.code:wire:
GET /v1/productos/42 HTTP/1.1

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
ETag: "a1b2c3"
{"id":42,"precio":38000}

# 2 minutos después (expiró), el navegador revalida:
GET /v1/productos/42 HTTP/1.1
If-None-Match: "a1b2c3"

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
ETag: "a1b2c3"
# sin body: el cliente usa su copia
sections.code:server:
import hashlib, json
from fastapi import Request, Response

@app.get("/v1/productos/{id}")
def obtener(id: int, request: Request, response: Response):
    p = repo.buscar(id)
    etag = '"' + hashlib.md5(json.dumps(p).encode()).hexdigest() + '"'
    if request.headers.get("if-none-match") == etag:
        return Response(status_code=304, headers={"ETag": etag})
    response.headers["ETag"] = etag
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "public, max-age=60"
    return p
sections.bad:
GET /v1/clientes/me
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600   ← el CDN la comparte entre usuarios
sections.good:
GET /v1/clientes/me
Cache-Control: private, no-cache        ← solo el navegador, y revalidando
sections.bridge:typescript: In the Network tab, the Size column shows (disk cache) or (memory cache) when the response did not touch the network, and the code 304 when there was a revalidation. The Disable cache checkbox exists precisely because these headers sometimes show you "stale" data during development.
sections.interview: HTTP caching is controlled with Cache-Control: max-age defines how long the response is fresh, public or private defines whether intermediaries like a CDN may store it or only the browser, no-cache forces revalidation and no-store forbids storing. To revalidate, the server sends an ETag, which is a fingerprint of the resource version; the client sends it back in If-None-Match and, if it did not change, gets a 304 with no body, which saves bandwidth. Caching happens in the browser, in proxies and in CDNs, and private data must never be marked as public.
sections.myths:
• no-cache does not mean "do not store": it means "store, but revalidate before using". The one that forbids storing is no-store.
  • Thinking only the browser caches. CDNs, reverse proxies and gateways do too.
  • Believing POST gets cached. In practice, only GET and HEAD.
